messages.body_plain:
I am trying to see if there are similar elements populated in the key and the values. And hence would like to know if I can send out multiple rhcollect function calls per key, value pair read in.

So this is what I am working with. I have a key and this key could potentially be featured in the value as well (in another key, value pair) . I want to see if a certain key is  part of a value in another key, value pair. So I am trying to rhcollect all the keys and also the value for every key, value pair.

pseudo code

for each key, value pair {
                rhcollect( key, key flag)
                rhcollect(value, value flag)
                                     }

Mind you, the keys and values are similar data. So I want to make a list of keys and a list of values. And then compare these two values to see if there are any common elements between them. For which I am trying to call rhcollect twice. With my initial runs this does not seem to occur.  Could anyone be kind enough to throw some light on this? Is it that rhcollect can be called only once per key, value pair? Or is there a way I could work around this?

Thanks in advance
Ashrith

messages.subject: Re: [rhipe] Installation problem with RhipeHbaseMozilla
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

So hopefully by the end of this email you can use RhipeHbaseCrash.

** Objective
   Read from Hbase (keys and values will be raw bytes), specifying start
   and stop rows,column families and their qualifiers.

** Getting
   Download the pre-build jar files from here:[1]
   Note, this jar files requires hbase-0.90.6.
   HBase classes *MUST* be present in classpath when your hadoop job runs.

** Using
   You need the code described at the end of this file.
   *** To read data from Hbase table

   #+BEGIN_SRC R
     sample.code <- rhmap({
       ## r is a list with entries called "data:json" and "meta:json"
       ## both entries are raw bytes
       ## k is rowkey and is also rawbytes
     })
     result <- rhwatch(map=sample.code
                       ,reduce=0                                   # For example
                       ,input=hbaseif(table="telemetry"            # pre-created table
                          ,colspec=c("data:json","meta:json")      # column family, qualifier
                          ,rows=list("20120601","20120602")        # row names as strings, otherwise must be raw
                          ,jars="/user/sguha/share/rhipecrashreport.jar"
                          ,zooinfo=list(zookeeper.znode.parent=A   # look in your hbase conf files for these
                             hbase.zookeeper.quorum=B)
                          ))

   #+END_SRC

   *** To write to a pre-made Hbase table

   #+BEGIN_SRC R
      sample.code <- rhmap({
        a <- list("data:json"=A,"meta:json"=B)
        rhcollect(rowkey, a)
        ## the values A and B will be serialized using RHIPE serialization
        ## same for rowkey
          })
     result <- rhwatch(map=sample.code
                       ,reduce=0
                       ,output=hbaseif(table="telemetry"
                          ,jars="/user/sguha/share/rhipecrashreport.jar"
                          ,zooinfo=list(zookeeper.znode.parent=A
                             hbase.zookeeper.quorum=B)
                          ))
   #+END_SRC R

[1] https://github.com/saptarshiguha/RhipeHbaseMozilla/blob/master/java/rhipecrashreport.jar?raw=true

hbase if function

##' @param table A string indicating tablename, If this used as an output, tablename must preexist, it wont be created
##' @param colspec Required for when this is called as input. Colspec is of the form c("family:label","family1:label1","family2:label2",...)
##' @param rows a list of two elements that has rowkey1, rowkey2. They can either be strings or raw bytes.
##' @param caching leave as default or see Java source for more explanation
##' @param cacheBlocks leave as default or see Java source for more explanation
##' @param autoReduceDetect if you have rhbase installed it will try and determine how many reduces to use. Needed only for output
##' @param jars location of rhipecrashreport.jar
##' @param zooinfo required and must be a list with entries of  zookeeper.znode.parent and hbase.zookeeper.quorum

hbasefmt <- function(table, colspec=NULL, rows=NULL,caching=3L, cacheBlocks=TRUE,autoReduceDetect=FALSE, jars="/user/sguha/share/rhipecrashreport.jar"
                     ,zooinfo){
  makeRaw <- function(a){
    a <- if(is.character(a)) charToRaw(a)
    if(!is.raw(a)) stop("rows must be raw")
    J("org.apache.commons.codec.binary.Base64")$encodeBase64String(.jbyte( a  ))
  }
  table <- eval(table); colspec <- eval(colspec);rows <- eval(rows);cacheBlocks <- eval(cacheBlocks)
  autoReduceDetect <- eval(autoReduceDetect)
  caching <- eval(caching)
  hbaseJars  <- list.files(Sys.getenv("HBASE_HOME"),pattern="jar$",full.names=TRUE,rec=TRUE)
  hbaseConf  <- list.files(sprintf("%s/conf",Sys.getenv("HBASE_HOME"),pattern="-site.xml$",full.names=TRUE,rec=TRUE))
  .jaddClassPath(c(hbaseJars,hbaseConf))
  function(mapred,direction, callers){
    if(direction=="output"){
      if(is.null(table)) stop("Please provide a pre-made table")
      if(autoReduceDetect){
        hb <-  rb.init()
        tba <- rb.table.connect(hb,table)
        mapred$mapred.reduce.tasks <- min(mapred$mapred.reduce.tasks,tba$table$getRegionsInfo()$size(),na.rm=TRUE)
      }
      mapred$hbase.mapred.outputtable <- as.character(table[1])
      mapred$zookeeper.znode.parent <- zooinfo$"zookeeper.znode.parent"
      mapred$hbase.zookeeper.quorum <- zooinfo$"hbase.zookeeper.quorum"
      mapred$rhipe_outputformat_class         = 'org.godhuli.rhipe.hbase.RHTableOutputFormat'
      mapred$rhipe_outputformat_keyclass <- 'org.godhuli.rhipe.RHBytesWritable'
      mapred$rhipe_outputformat_valueclass <- 'org.godhuli.rhipe.RHBytesWritable'
      mapred$rhipe_map_output_keyclass <- 'org.godhuli.rhipe.RHBytesWritable'
      mapred$rhipe_map_output_valueclass <- 'org.godhuli.rhipe.RHBytesWritable'
      mapred$jarfiles <- jars
      mapred
    }else{
      if(is.null(table)) stop("Please provide table type e.g. crash_reports or telemetry")
      mapred$rhipe.hbase.tablename <- as.character(table[1])
      mapred$rhipe.hbase.colspec <- paste(colspec,collapse=",")
      if(!is.null(rows)){
        mapred$rhipe.hbase.rowlim.start <- makeRaw(rows[[1]])
        mapred$rhipe.hbase.rowlim.end   <- makeRaw(rows[[2]])
      }
      mapred$rhipe.hbase.mozilla.cacheblocks <- sprintf("%s:%s",as.integer(caching),as.integer(cacheBlocks))
      mapred$zookeeper.znode.parent <- zooinfo$"zookeeper.znode.parent"
      mapred$hbase.zookeeper.quorum <- zooinfo$"hbase.zookeeper.quorum"
      message(sprintf("Using %s table", table))
      if(!table %in% c("telemetry","crash_reports")){
        mapred$rhipe_inputformat_class         = 'org.godhuli.rhipe.hbase.RHHBaseGeneral'
      }else{
        if(table=="crash_reports"){
          mapred$rhipe.hbase.dateformat <- "yyMMdd"
        }else if(table =="telemetry"){
          mapred$rhipe.hbase.dateformat <- "yyyyMMdd"
        }
        mapred$rhipe.hbase.mozilla.prefix <- if (table=="telemetry") "byteprefix"  else "hexprefix"
        mapred$rhipe_inputformat_class <- 'org.godhuli.rhipe.hbase.RHCrashReportTableInputFormat'
      }
      ## mapred$hbase.client.scanner.caching <- 100L
      mapred$rhipe_inputformat_keyclass <- 'org.godhuli.rhipe.RHBytesWritable'
      mapred$rhipe_inputformat_valueclass <- 'org.godhuli.rhipe.hbase.RHResult'
      mapred$jarfiles <- jars
      mapred
    }
  }
}

Oh sorry, I mean I am using Rhipe 0.73.

hbasemap is a function that read data from hbase. Here is sample code.

hbasemap <- function(tablename, colspec,
rows,dateformat="yyyyMMdd",cacheBlocks=3L, caching=TRUE){
  mapred <- list()
  mapred$rhipe.hbase.tablename <- as.character(tablename[1])
  mapred$rhipe.hbase.colspec <- paste(colspec,collapse=",")
  mapred$rhipe.hbase.rowlim.start <-rows[1]
  mapred$rhipe.hbase.rowlim.end <- rows[2]
  mapred$rhipe.hbase.mozilla.dateformat <- "yyyyMMdd"
  mapred$rhipe.hbase.mozilla.cacheblocks <- sprintf("%s:%s",
as.integer(cacheBlocks), tolower(as.character(caching)))

library(Rhipe)
rhinit()

hbasemap <- function(tablename, colspec, rows,caching=3L, cacheBlocks=TRUE){
  ## This function can be used when ever accessing Hbase

  mapred <- list()
  mapred$rhipe.hbase.tablename <- as.character(tablename[1])
  mapred$rhipe.hbase.colspec <- paste(colspec,collapse=",")
  mapred$rhipe.hbase.rowlim.start <-rows[1]
  mapred$rhipe.hbase.rowlim.end <- rows[2]

  mapred$rhipe.hbase.mozilla.cacheblocks <- sprintf("%s:%s",as.integer(caching),as.integer(cacheBlocks))
  mapred$rhipe.hbase.mozilla.prefix <- "byteprefix"
  mapred$rhipe_inputformat_class <- 'org.godhuli.rhipe.hbase.RHCrashReportTableInputFormat'
  mapred$rhipe_inputformat_keyclass <- 'org.godhuli.rhipe.RHBytesWritable'
  mapred$rhipe_inputformat_valueclass <- 'org.godhuli.rhipe.hbase.RHResult'
  mapred
}

####Map function to get key and value#######################
map <- expression({
   lapply(seq_along(map.values), function(r) {
      v <- map.values[[r]]

      k <- map.keys[[r]]
      rhcollect(k, mean(v))
   })
})

#######Reduce function to sort and shuffle######################
reduce <- expression(
   pre={
      mean <- 0

   },
 reduce={
      mean <- max(mean, unlist(reduce.values))
   },

      rhcollect(reduce.key, mean)
   }

)

Hello,

>could we define row-key and leave column qualifier null.

If you download (updated now) :
https://github.com/saptarshiguha/RhipeHbaseMozilla/blob/master/java/rhipecrashreport.jar?raw=true
then you can set colspec="" and you get all col families and column
qualifiers.

Your rowkey is a string. Is this a Java string? HBase stores rowkeys as raw bytes
and hence is critical that you pass the right bytes. the hbaseif function behaves

- if the key is a string, hbaseif converts it to bytes using charToRaw
- otherwise the key *must* be a raw vector - it is upto the user to convert it to raw bytes

so rowkey (and *use argument names* in the function call)
hbaseif(..., rows=list(key1,key2))

messages.subject: Re: how to get mapper to run multiple times
messages.subject_clean: how to get mapper to run multiple times
messages.body_plain:
On Thursday, June 21, 2012 1:50:04 AM UTC+5:30, dtenenba wrote:

> Hello,
> I changed some of the Rhipe examples from the github wiki to do what I want to do, and it works, but it looks like the mapper only runs once, instead of once per piece of input data which is what I would like.
> It's also possible that the way I have put my code together is not well thought-out.
>
> What I did was change the word count generator example to generate some strings of input data to process.
> Then I created another mapreduce job, based on the word count example (with no reduce function, because I don't need one) which takes a piece of that input data and does some processing to it and then writes out some output.
> It works but it seems, judging from the output, that the mapper only ran once.
>
> I realize that maybe I should change this to a single mapreduce job, where the mapper runs just once and creates all the input data, and the reducer processes it. I have tried that and run into problems. So I thought it would be best to post about what actually works and ask how I can get it to work the proper number of times, and then maybe incrementally get to a better way of doing it.
>
> So first, off, some dependencies are required in order to do this, if you want to try it yourself:
> You must be running R-2.15.
> Do the following:

> source("http://bioconductor.org/biocLite.R")
> useDevel()

> biocLite(c("snpStats", "VariantAnnotation", "TxDb.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg19.knownGene"))
>
> Outside of R, do this (because this package is not part of Bioconductor):
> svn co --username readonly --password readonly https://hedgehog.fhcrc.org/bioconductor/trunk/madman/Rpacks/BiocCloud/
> R CMD INSTALL BiocCloud
> (if the above step complains about missing dependencies, install them)
>
> Now, here is what actually works:
>
> Step 1, generate input data:
>
> library(Rhipe)
> rhinit()
>
> makeDataSet <- function(N, dest, local=TRUE)
> {
>     map <- as.expression(bquote({
>         N <- .(N)
>         urls <- getBucketUrls()
>         txdb <- TxDb.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg19.knownGene
>         cds <- cds(txdb)

messages.body_plain:
Let me see if I understand correctly.

1) You have a file with N lines in text.
2) Processing each of the N lines is a lengthy amount of work so you want to it divided into M different chunks so that one mapper isn't working all N lines.  M may be N (the number of lines) or the number of simultaneous mappers you can run or some multiple of the number of mappers you can run.

This job has the characteristic that N is very small, but it implies tons of processing time, so what you can't do is leave the block size of the HDFS determine how the mappers get allocated work.

This is a use case we have thought a fair bit about in the past, but because I haven't been using Rhipe for about 6 months I forget exactly what is most effective. I believe the trick is to do it in the reduce, but that can depend on how your cluster is setup.

For example,
Map: each line goes to a key
Reduce: process the line as an input as you were doing before in the map but now in the "reduce$post" part of the reduce expression.

The thing you have to worry about is how the cluster is spreading out the reduce work.  Sometimes hadoop doesn't do what you expect in terms of spreading out very small starting inputs because of "details", and also different clusters have different maximum number of reducers they are configured to use, so this may not be effectively using a cluster set up for many mappers to few reducers.

Good luck,
Jeremiah

messages.body_plain:
I think this is an old question that has been answered.
Use Rhipe_0.73.1 (see code/ directory in Rhipe github)

rhwatch(map, ..., input=rhfmt(type='text', folders="path to input folders", nline=number of lines to process at one time e.g. 10)

if nline = 10, then each mapper will process 10 lines, so if you have 1000 lines and nline==10, then you should have 100 map.tasks.

> >     genome <- line[5]

> >

messages.subject: rhipe and hadoop fair scheduler
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I have a CDH3 env implemented with fair-schelduling, everything works fine until
I have the scenario whereby an application is running which currently has been allocated
all the resources available on the cluster. Under normal circumstances, the next job submitted
will then work to get its fair share of resources and it too, will start to run with the fair scheduler
properly allocating the resources.

For rhipe, if I submit the job and it is the first job to ask for the resources, the job will run without
any issues, even if another job comes in and starts to get its fair share of resources, the jobs will
run just fine (I've had up to 8 running, each with the fair share of resources)

If there is another job already using the resources and I start up an R job it will fail to start and will
not attempt to run, generating failed statuses for each task.

It seems as long as rhipe can get its request and not get queued up, that everything is fine, but as
soon as it needs to compete for the resources it will not start or queue.

Am I missing a rhipe configuration parameter, I looked through all the basic ones, but did not
find one that would address this.

thanks,

Jim

messages.body_plain:
RHIPE is really Hadoop Streaming very customized. I see the issue is during the
Reduce phase. I don't think there is a RHIPE option for this per se, rather some
Hadoop option. We regularly have 10-15 jobs running on our cluster and i don't
see these errors.

keep in mind, RHIPE launches an R process for every task (it would be possible
to launch once per JVM, but it's tricky to find out when the JVM shuts down)

Cheers
Saptarshi

messages.subject: Re: rhipe and hadoop fair scheduler
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I'm not sure about the reduce phase, I am testing this with an R job that only
maps. This particular issue didn't start occurring until the fair-scheduler was
introduced, no other applications that run M/R have any issues, and it is only
if an application is running that currently owns the resources and the scheduler
needs to re-allocate them to rhipe that rhipe gets upset and generates the
errors. If the rhipe job is running already, it will give up the resources it owns
to the FS (there are some high priority jobs that must run and are very aggressive
at getting their resources), but the rhipe job will continue on and complete without any
issues, even rescheduling those tasks that were killed by the high priority jobs and
completing those as well.

My first thought is that rhipe is not waiting until the resources are free, the wait time
I have set is 180s before rhipe can get aggressive and demand the resources.

I will look at the FS and streaming jobs more closely.

Jim

On Monday, April 29, 2013 11:23:03 AM UTC-4, Jim Langston wrote:
> Hi,
>
> I have a CDH3 env implemented with fair-schelduling, everything works fine until
> I have the scenario whereby an application is running which currently has been allocated
> all the resources available on the cluster. Under normal circumstances, the next job submitted
> will then work to get its fair share of resources and it too, will start to run with the fair scheduler
> properly allocating the resources.
>
> For rhipe, if I submit the job and it is the first job to ask for the resources, the job will run without
> any issues, even if another job comes in and starts to get its fair share of resources, the jobs will
> run just fine (I've had up to 8 running, each with the fair share of resources)
>
> If there is another job already using the resources and I start up an R job it will fail to start and will
> not attempt to run, generating failed statuses for each task.
>
> It seems as long as rhipe can get its request and not get queued up, that everything is fine, but as
> soon as it needs to compete for the resources it will not start or queue.
>
> Am I missing a rhipe configuration parameter, I looked through all the basic ones, but did not
> find one that would address this.
